responses.review_design:1:6: fixed: the residual is fixed together with 2:1. The resume (4.2) compares the worktree with the conflicted tree T, not with HEAD: `git diff --name-only -z T --` for modified/deleted paths plus `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z` for untracked ones, and any path outside the listed files re-blocks, listing them. The merge tree is built in a temporary index (read-tree T, then `git --literal-pathspecs add -A -- <listed files>`, write-tree), so only the listed files from the worktree enter the merge and whatever the agent staged is ignored. Test 1 covers scratch, *.orig and non-listed edits.
responses.review_design:1:7: fixed: the residual is fixed together with 2:2. The scope now also covers the PR title and the trunk commit that the merge op writes. The PR title is c2's subject (edited when it differs), and the merge op passes an explicit conventional --subject/--body to gh pr merge: squash gets c2's subject + ' (#n)' with c1's and c2's bodies and the breaking footers; merge gets `chore(merge): G<g> <title> (#<pr>)`; rebase gets no flags. D10's false 'only branches whose commits reach trunk' reason is replaced. 4.8, SPEC §4.14/§5.5 and test 10 (one case per method) are updated. Owner's words kept verbatim in 2.1.
responses.review_design:2:1: fixed: as suggested, and checked on Git 2.55.0 (section 10): after read-tree -u --reset T, an edit of a.txt and a hand-staged t.txt, git status shows `MM a.txt` and `M  t.txt`, while `git diff --name-only -z T --` shows only a.txt, and ls-files --others shows the untracked scratch file. The temporary-index build gives the resolved a.txt and trunk's t.txt. Revision 2 also misplaced --literal-pathspecs, which is a global git option (`git --literal-pathspecs add`); that is corrected too. Test 1 adds a case where trunk also changes a non-conflicting file (and the agent staged it) and the first resume is accepted.
responses.review_design:2:2: fixed: same fix as 1:7. 4.8 covers trunk merge commits, with the true reason: gh pr merge writes its own trunk commit, whose subject defaults to the PR title. Under squash the explicit c2 subject keeps the derived type and `!`, so semantic-release gets the same release as from c1+c2, and 4.5.2's claim holds. Under merge, chore(merge) releases nothing and c1/c2 still land as the second parent. Manual GitHub merges are noted: the PR title is conventional, and REPAIR.md says to set the merge-commit default to the PR title. The fake gh records --subject/--body, and test 10 checks that every trunk subject is conventional for each method.
responses.review_design:2:3: fixed: merge mode is sticky per branch (4.1). Before any rebase, abort or push, base lists `chore(sync):` merges with a Zzzops-Old-Base trailer on `rev-list --first-parent --merges W ^base_commit`. If there is one and the policy does not require merge_sync, base blocks {category: policy, waiting_for: human, reason: 'work branch has merge syncs'}, asks for merge_sync to be restored, and pushes nothing. D9's 'never' claim is narrowed to 'while the policy requires it'. Section 8, merge_sync.txt, SPEC §4.5/§8, DESIGN's upgrade recipe and REPAIR's rollback state that removing merge_sync is not supported while any open goal's work branch has merge syncs, because older engines cannot be stopped otherwise. Test 8 adds the case.

output.summary: Revision 3 builds on revision 2 and fixes only the three open round-2 items. The conflict resume compares the worktree with the conflicted tree T (git diff --name-only T plus ls-files --others), not git status against HEAD, and builds the merge from the listed files in a temporary index (verified on Git 2.55.0). Conventional commits now also cover the PR title (c2's subject) and the trunk commit that the merge op writes: squash gets c2's subject and the bodies, merge gets chore(merge): G<g> <title> (#<pr>), rebase gets nothing. Merge mode is sticky per work branch: without merge_sync in the policy, a branch that has sync merges blocks base with a policy item instead of being rebased, and removing merge_sync while such branches are open is documented as unsupported.

findings.text: §6 answers an older G1039 draft, and four of G1039 rev 1's six §5 items don't match. (1) G1039 calls unchanged(node, old_cp, new_cp) and reads 'the checkpoint's recorded scope'; G1038 defines clean(node, k, r, cp2, scope) with the scope from checkpoint_scope(graph, node, record). (3) G1039 relies on a stored checkpoint scope key, which D3 rejects, so G1039's predicate would always run unscoped and stale test_design whenever implementation lines move. (4) G1039 reads base output sync = {from, onto, merge, resolved}, including sync.from in §3.4; G1038 writes synced = {old, onto, work, tip, merge, resolved}. (6) G1039 describes the interdiff as 'range-diff plus previous.syncs'; G1038 drops range-diff for log -p --first-parent --no-merges plus previous.syncs. §6's left column also quotes needs G1039 rev 1 no longer has (relocate(node, key, cp, synced); Done.synced = {old, onto, tip}). Fix: rewrite §6 against G1039 rev 1 §5 items 1-6; pin one name, signature and key set (for example unchanged(node, k, old_cp, new_cp, scope), with the scope passed in from checkpoint_scope and never stored, and output key synced with old); state the exact edits G1039 must make (no scope key, synced.old not sync.from, the interdiff form) so the root can relay them. Otherwise two goals that each pass review are built against a carry interface neither one implements.

The own-commit walk P..W (§4.5: c2's type and '!', the body's subjects, the BREAKING CHANGE footers, authors and dates) picks up foreign commits whenever onto does not descend from the old base. That happens with a rewritten dependency PR head (routine under G1038, since every re-integrate re-squashes the PR branch), a dropped dependency, or a G1025 target change. D1 keeps the tree right, but M = commit-tree -p tip -p onto keeps the old base in first-parent history, so log --first-parent P..W walks into old dependency commits, or into all dev history not on release/N. Example: a dev 'feat!:' lands in a hotfix's c2 and forces a major bump on the line. Fix: exclude every previous base, not just P. For example, record the old base as a trailer in each engine merge message, then walk --first-parent --no-merges W ^P ^<each merge's second parent> ^<each recorded old base>. Add test-6 cases that assert the c2 subject and body.

c2's type derivation does not match release.config.cjs, so 'semantic-release computes the same release bump' is false in some cases. revert releases a patch, but the order 'feat > fix > perf > any other > chore' puts revert in an unordered 'other' bucket, so a revert: + refactor: goal can get refactor: and no release. The walk also counts test_design's commits (test:, fix(test):). Fix: rank by release effect (breaking > feat > fix/perf/revert > no release); derive c2's type from implementation commits only (those touching paths outside F, the split §4.5 already uses for identity); c1 is always test:. Test the revert case.

R1's premise is factually wrong. Outside branching mode nothing re-syncs base when dev moves (G1025 §2: G1021 keeps base non-stale on dev moves), and in branching mode G1025 pass 3 fires only before agent phases of unstacked goals, never before ops (G1025 §5.3, D1). So 'at integrate time, in the normal flow, the last synced trunk commit is the live tip' does not hold, and the PR routinely sits on an older trunk commit. The conclusion is still defensible: today's integrate already rebuilds on ctx.inputs['base'], the PR tree equals the tested tree, PR CI and GitHub check the real merge, and BEHIND/CONFLICTING come back to base. Fix: restate R1 with that reasoning; reword outcome §1 and test 5 to 'on the trunk commit of the last sync (today's behaviour)', and say explicitly that this is how acceptance 3's 'trunk tip' is met.

§8 and D9 claim an older engine 'would refuse a work branch with merges (I1/I2) ... fails closed'. That is false for base. At dev, base.py runs wt.sync, then 'rebase -q --onto onto old', which drops the merges and replays the pre-sync commits (redoing their conflicts); then check_i1_i2(onto, H) on the linearised result, which passes; then a non-fast-forward push (W, H), the rewrite this goal removes. Old agent submits also pass, because check_i1_i2(W, head) covers only the agent's own range. Only an old integrate fails closed. Workers here run cached plugin engines, so this window is real. Fix: make the policy step a precondition. Either the new engine writes a merge sync only when settings.engine.requires contains merge_sync (otherwise base blocks with a policy-prerequisite item), or state the rule that the merge_sync policy lands before the first merge-synced base runs. Correct §8 and D9, and add a test.

findings.response: fixed: the resume (4.2) refuses when git status --untracked-files=all shows any path outside the listed files (re-blocks listing them), and then stages only the listed files with git add -A --literal-pathspecs -- <files>. Test 1 covers an untracked scratch file, a *.orig file and an edit to a non-listed file.
findings.text: The conflict resume (§4.2) runs 'git add -A', so anything in the worktree goes into the merge commit, and from there into the goal's code and its squashed PR: untracked scratch files, *.orig files from mergetool, build output, edits to files that did not conflict. Fix: stage only the listed files (git add -A -- <files>); re-block if any other path differs from T, listing those paths, and refuse untracked or modified files outside the list. Cover this in test 1.

findings.response: fixed: adopted the owner's decision, recorded verbatim in 2.1, in 4.8 and D10. Covered: every commit on work, stack and PR branches, agent- and engine-made. Exempt: record commits on goal refs (zzzops: answer G<g> ..., parsed by G1026) and lease refs, because they are machine-parsed and never reach trunk. Submit refuses non-conventional subjects (commit_subject) and non-test commits from the preserved node (test_commit_type), and implement commits touching frozen paths (test_freeze, now per commit); codes, texts and the SPEC §4.14 text are given. Engine subjects become chore(sync): merge <onto> into G<g> and chore(stack): combine/partial combine for G<g>; integrate's commits are test: and the derived type (4.5.2). Test 10 covers both refusals and the engine subjects; test 5 covers the type derivation.
findings.text: Owner decision, relayed by the root (material). Owner, verbatim: "Yeah, we should ensure we always use conventional commit messages". This was in reply to the root's proposal: keep the tests/implementation split by recorded frozen paths and per-phase submit ranges, not by commit message; (1) submit refuses commits whose subjects are not conventional commits, test_design's commits must be test:, and implement's commits must not touch frozen paths; (2) integrate's squashed tests commit is 'test: ...' and the implementation commit's type is derived from the goal's commits. The design must adopt this and state which commits the rule covers. The root recommends: every commit on work and PR branches, agent-made and engine-made (docs(review): commits already comply); engine record commits on goal refs ('zzzops: answer G<g> ...', which G1026 parses) keep their machine subjects because they never reach trunk; justify any other scope. G1038's own engine commits do not comply: the sync merge 'Merge <onto> into zzzops/work/g<g> (zzzops base)' (§4.1), and the combine commits 'zzzops: stack for G<g> ...' / 'zzzops: partial stack' (base.py combine) on the stack branches PRs target. Give them conventional subjects (for example chore(sync): ..., chore(stack): ...) or exclude them with a reason. Add the submit refusal codes and texts, the SPEC §4.14 text, tests for both refusals and for the engine subjects, and the type derivation from the implementation commits' conventional types.

Still open on review_design:1:6: the 4.2 resume check 2 (`git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all` lists no path outside the listed files) always re-blocks. After `git read-tree -u --reset T` the index is T and HEAD stays at the tip, so status reports every path where T differs from the tip (every trunk-side change) as a staged modification. Verified on Git 2.55.0: trunk changes a.txt and t.txt, the goal changes a.txt; after read-tree and editing a.txt, status prints `MM a.txt` and `M  t.txt`, while `git diff --name-only T` prints only a.txt. Fix: compare against T: `git diff --name-only -z T --` (worktree vs T, whatever the agent staged) plus `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z` for untracked paths, and refuse any path outside the listed files. Add a test-1 case where trunk also changes a non-conflicting file and the resume is accepted.

Still open on review_design:1:7, one residual: D10 and 4.8 justify the scope with 'these are the only branches whose commits reach trunk', which is false. The merge op runs `gh pr merge --<method>` (merge.py:92), which writes a trunk commit whose subject is the PR title, not a conventional subject. dev's tip f4eaf74 'Replace ENGINE_VERSION and engine.min with declared engine capabilities (G1027) (#759)' is one. Under merge.method `merge` this adds a non-conventional commit per goal to dev and main, against the owner's 'always'. Under `squash`, which the policy allows and section 3 mentions, GitHub writes one commit titled with the PR title, so semantic-release sees no conventional commit and c2's derived type and release are lost, which breaks the 4.5.2 claim. Fix: the merge op passes --subject/--body to gh pr merge: for squash, c2's subject and a body with c1's and c2's bodies and the breaking footers; for merge, a conventional subject such as `chore(merge): <PR title> (#n)`; for rebase, nothing. Add this to 4.8's covered list, SPEC §4.14/§5.5 and a test-10 case per method, or exempt trunk merge commits with a true reason and still fix the squash case.

N1: D9's 'no older engine can ever see a merge-synced branch' fails on the documented rollback. SPEC's upgrade procedure at f4eaf74 says 'Rollback is the same procedure removing the names'. Once merge_sync is removed from settings.engine.requires, the new engine's mode becomes rebase (4.1) and older engines un-pause, and both run today's `rebase -q --onto onto old` on a work branch with chore(sync): merges: the merges are dropped, every resolved conflict is redone and the branch is force-pushed. That is the review_design:1:5 hazard again. Fix: make merge mode sticky per branch. If W's first-parent history above base_commit has an engine sync merge and the policy does not require merge_sync, base blocks with a policy item ('the work branch has merge syncs; the policy must require merge_sync') and pushes nothing. merge_sync.txt and SPEC §4.5/§8 state that removing merge_sync is not supported while an open goal's work branch has merge syncs. Add a test-8 case.

output.summary: Round 2: F1-F5 resolved. The section 6 G1039 contract can be adopted as written; the own-commit walk via Zzzops-Old-Base trailers, the release-ranked c2 type, the restated R1 and the merge_sync precondition were all checked against f4eaf74 (G1027 merged). The new date and idempotence rule is sound. Still open: F6, because the resume's git status check compares against HEAD (the tip), so every trunk-side change in T counts as an unlisted path and the resume always re-blocks (verified on Git 2.55); F7, because trunk merge commits from the merge op (PR-title subjects) are outside the conventional scope on a false premise, and under merge.method squash c2's type is lost. New: N1, the documented rollback (removing merge_sync from requires) puts the new and older engines back to rebasing merge-synced branches.

spec:
Found while dogfooding Release 1. Two pieces of machinery caused most of the friction in the G1022–G1028 run:
- Syncing a goal with the integration branch is a rebase. Conflict resolutions are not kept, so each later rebase redoes them, and a rebase rewrites the work branch.
- The frozen tests are the diff up to the tests checkpoint, and the implementation is everything after it, so a test fix found after implement has to be inserted before the implementation commits. That needs a history rewrite and a force-push of the work branch, which only the owner could run. It happened four times (G1025, G1026, G1027 twice).

Owner decisions (verbatim):
- "For updating the branch with the trunk, I think merges might work better as conflict resolution doesn't get lost. Then maybe a final rebase when integrating in order to clean up the history?"
- On the integrate history, the owner chose "Squash to tests + code" over rebasing with reused resolutions or keeping the merges: integrate collapses the goal into two commits (tests, implementation) on the trunk tip.
- "I think we may as well get these done now, before dogfooding again"

Scope:
- `base` (and any scheduled sync) brings trunk into the goal's work branch with a merge commit, never a rebase or force-push. A conflicting merge becomes a base finding as G1021 does today.
- test_design may add tests commits after implementation commits. Which tests are frozen, and which diff is the implementation, are computed from paths and checkpoints rather than commit order, so no history rewrite is ever needed during a goal.
- integrate produces the PR branch as exactly two commits on the integration tip: the goal's tests and its implementation (plus the review records the engine already carries, if they must stay separate). The work branch is left as is.
- No owner-run force-push is needed at any point in a goal's normal flow.

Acceptance:
- A goal whose trunk moves twice during delivery syncs by two merges; the second sync does not redo the first sync's conflict resolution.
- A test fix submitted by test_design after implement committed is accepted without any rewrite; implement may not edit it; review_impl sees only implementation changes.
- The PR for such a goal has exactly the tests commit and the implementation commit on the trunk tip, and its tree equals the work branch merged with trunk.
- This PR edits docs/design/SPEC.md and DESIGN.md for every contract change it makes and adds a HISTORY §4 row.
title: Sync goal branches with trunk by merge, squash at integrate, and let test fixes land after implementation
